prs.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
prs.author: adityuhkapoor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py decides whether to json.loads() a string input value based on the field's type annotation. The original check was only `field_info.annotation is not str`, which fails to account for union annotations that include str (most commonly `str | None`, the idiomatic way to make an optional string parameter). As a result, a valid string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON-encoded payload passed as a plain string parameter, or any string containing `{...}`/`[...]`) gets silently decoded into a dict/list and corrupts the caller's intended string value. Both PRs replace that single equality check with a smarter union-aware helper in the exact same conditional in pre_parse_json. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: All three restructure async_auth_flow to release the lock before yielding the protected request and only reacquire it around the 401/403 handling. 3243 goes further by replacing anyio.Lock with anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) for both the state lock and the new second flow-control lock, with an explicit rationale: anyio.Lock enforces same-task acquire/release, but httpx can resume or close the async_auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that originally yielded it, which can raise at release time. clusters.pick_reason: All three restructure async_auth_flow to release the lock before yielding the protected request and only reacquire it around the 401/403 handling. 3243 goes further by replacing anyio.Lock with anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) for both the state lock and the new second flow-control lock, with an explicit rationale: anyio.Lock enforces same-task acquire/release, but httpx can resume or close the async_auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that originally yielded it, which can raise at release time. Neither #2858 (which adds a second anyio.Lock named refresh_lock for single-flight refresh) nor #3252 (which keeps the single original anyio.Lock and just narrows its scope) changes the lock type, so both remain exposed to that same cross-task release case that 3243 specifically targets.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` off the pre-existing `str(message.id)` cast, which carries a latent bug: JSON-RPC ids `1` (int) and `"1"` (string) are distinct per spec but collapse to the same string key, and a string id equal to `_GET_stream` would collide with the standalone GET stream's slot. #3221 replaces the key with a new `_request_stream_key()` helper that type-prefixes ids (`i:`/`s:`), fixing the duplicate-id race without introducing false-positive 409s on distinct same-looking ids or the GET-stream key collision that #3063's simpler approach leaves unresolved.

clusters.pick_reason: All three restructure async_auth_flow to release the lock before yielding the protected request and only reacquire it around the 401/403 handling. 3243 goes further by replacing anyio.Lock with anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) for both the state lock and the new second flow-control lock, with an explicit rationale: anyio.Lock enforces same-task acquire/release, but httpx can resume or close the async_auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that originally yielded it, which can raise at release time. Neither #2858 (which adds a second anyio.Lock named refresh_lock for single-flight refresh) nor #3252 (which keeps the single original anyio.Lock and just narrows its scope) changes the lock type, so both remain exposed to that same cross-task release case that 3243 specifically targets.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` off the pre-existing `str(message.id)` cast, which carries a latent bug: JSON-RPC ids `1` (int) and `"1"` (string) are distinct per spec but collapse to the same string key, and a string id equal to `_GET_stream` would collide with the standalone GET stream's slot. #3221 replaces the key with a new `_request_stream_key()` helper that type-prefixes ids (`i:`/`s:`), fixing the duplicate-id race without introducing false-positive 409s on distinct same-looking ids or the GET-stream key collision that #3063's simpler approach leaves unresolved.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses (one request receives the other's payload, the other hangs). Both PRs add a check that rejects a second in-flight request whose id is already in use.
